BURHAN:v1p206/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.speaker: عائشة
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.claim: The beginning-of-revelation report in al-Bukhari, explicitly authenticated by al-Hakim from Aisha, establishes اقرأ as the first revelation; Muslim gives it through “He taught man what he did not know.”
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.anchor: وأخرجه الحاكم فى مستدركه من حديث عائشة رضى الله عنها صريحا وقال صحيح الإسناد

ITQAN:v1p75/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.claim: Ubayd b. ʿUmayr says Gabriel brought the Prophet a silk sheet and told him to recite; he identifies the opening of al-ʿAlaq as the first sura sent down.
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أشتة في كتاب المصاحف عن عبيد بن عمير قال جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بنمط فقال اقرأ

ITQAN:v1p75/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.speaker: الزهري
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.claim: Al-Zuhrī recounts that while the Prophet was at Ḥirāʾ, an angel brought a silk sheet inscribed with the opening verses of al-ʿAlaq.
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.anchor: وأخرج عن الزهري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذ أتى ملك بنمط من ديباج فيه مكتوب

BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r3.claim: Iqra is a command, repeated to reinforce the obligation and introduce a new sentence about the most generous Lord; a permissible pause follows خلق because the Prophet had objected that he could not read.
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r3.anchor: وكرر علامة الأمر بالقراءة تأكيدا للإيجاب وتمهيدا لما يعقبه من قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r4.claim: God is more generous than every generous person, gives without motive or desire for praise, and is the source from whom all others receive generosity.
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r4.anchor: وهو الأكرم أي الزائد في الكرم على كل كريم فإنه ينعم بلا غرض ولا يطلب مدحا

BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r5.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r5.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh parses ربك as the subject, الأكرم as its adjective, and the relative clause as its predicate.
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r5.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ : ربك مبتدأ والأكرم صفته والذي مع صلته خبر

QASHANI:96:3-8/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:3-8/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:3-8/r1.claim: God is unsurpassably generous, having gifted the Prophet His essence and attributes; He would not leave him annihilated without restoring existence, since otherwise no generosity or attribute would appear.
QASHANI:96:3-8/r1.anchor: البالغ إلى النهاية في الكرم الذي لا يمكن فوق غايته كرم لجوده بذاته وصفاته وهب لك ذاته وصفاته

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r7.claim: Al-akram means generous, or the most generous of every generous one.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r7.anchor: الأكرم ( : أي الكريم . ويقال : الأكرم من كل كريم

IBNASHUR:96:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:3/r1.claim: The second iqraʾ repeats the first to emphasize the command.
IBNASHUR:96:3/r1.anchor: تأكيد ل { اقرأ } الأول للاهتمام بهذا الأمر

IBNASHUR:96:3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:3/r2.claim: The sentence “your Lord is the Most Generous” begins an explanatory answer to how the Prophet can read when he lacks literacy; the One who taught by the pen can teach him.
IBNASHUR:96:3/r2.anchor: فالمعنى أن الذي علّم الناس الكتابة بالقلم والقراءة قادر على أن يعلمك القراءة وأنت لا تعلم الكتابة

IBNASHUR:96:3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:3/r3.claim: Read alongside ʿĀʾishah's revelation report and Gabriel's repeated command, the sentence answers the Prophet's “I cannot read”: knowledge can come through dictation, instruction, or inspiration.
IBNASHUR:96:3/r3.anchor: عن قوله لجبريل : « ما أنا بقارىء » فالمعنى

IBNASHUR:96:3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:3/r4.claim: God taught Adam the names even though Adam was not a reader, illustrating knowledge imparted without literacy.
IBNASHUR:96:3/r4.anchor: وقد علم الله آدم الأسماء ولم يكن آدم قارئاً

IBNASHUR:96:3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:3/r5.claim: The expected pronoun is replaced by rabbuka to emphasize divine care and to keep the Lord-title connected to the command to read in His name.
IBNASHUR:96:3/r5.anchor: لتأكيد ما يشعر به { ربّك } من العناية

IBNASHUR:96:3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:3/r6.claim: Al-akram intensifies generosity rather than comparing God with others; karam is giving the recipient beneficial gifts, including existence, creation, and sustenance.
IBNASHUR:96:3/r6.anchor: مصوغ للدلالة على قوة الاتصاف بالكرم وليس مصوغاً للمفاضلة

IBNASHUR:96:3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:3/r7.claim: The opening five verses gather divine attributes: Lordship entails existence and oneness; creation and teaching entail action; the Most Generous conveys perfection and freedom from defect.
IBNASHUR:96:3/r7.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه الآيات الخمس من أول السورة أصول الصفات الإلهية

IBNASHUR:96:3/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:3/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:3/r8.claim: The two objects of “taught by the pen” are omitted and understood as teaching writers or people how to write.
IBNASHUR:96:3/r8.anchor: محذوفان دل عليهما قوله : { بالقلم } وتقديره : علّم الكاتبين

IBNASHUR:96:3/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:3/r9.speaker: أبو حية النميري
IBNASHUR:96:3/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyah al-Numayrī's verse uses a Jew's hand writing as evidence for the association of writing with the People of the Book.
IBNASHUR:96:3/r9.anchor: قال أبو حية النُّميري : كما خُطّ الكتابُ

IBNASHUR:96:3/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:3/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:3/r10.claim: The account says writing first appeared among Arabs in al-Anbār; Ḥarb ibn Umayyah brought it to the Ḥijāz from Aslam ibn Sidrah, who learned it from Murāmir ibn Murrah; Ḥimyar had an earlier script called Musnad.
IBNASHUR:96:3/r10.anchor: وذُكر أن ظهور الخط في العرب أول ما كان عند أهل الأنبار

IBNASHUR:96:3/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:3/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:3/r11.claim: The relative clause is placed between subject and predicate to answer the Prophet's fear that he could not read because he could not write: God can teach him reading.
IBNASHUR:96:3/r11.anchor: اعتذار عن تعذر امتثال أمره بقوله : { اقرأ } ؛

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.claim: Aisha narrates in the two Sahihs that Gabriel came to Muhammad in Hira, commanded him three times, embraced him forcefully each time, then recited the opening through 'what he did not know.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.anchor: وفي حديث ( الصحيحين ) عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قولها فيه : ( حتى جاءه الحق وهو في غار حراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.claim: Aisha's narration is directly from the Prophet; her account that he returned trembling with the passage means he retained and recited what had been dictated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.anchor: فهذا الحديث روته عائشة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقولها قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.claim: Khadija's request that Waraqa hear him further indicates Muhammad recited the revealed passage immediately; Gabriel's repeated command repeated God's wording to accustom him to reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.anchor: وهذا ينبىء بأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عندما قيل له بعد الفطة الثالثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.claim: The opening five verses gather divine attributes: lordship implies existence and oneness, creation and teaching indicate acts, and al-Akram entails perfection and freedom from deficiency.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه الآيات الخمس من أول السورة أصول الصفات الإلاهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.claim: These are the final five verses of the passage first revealed at Hira; the following discussion on verses 6–10 begins a new subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.anchor: وهذه آخر الخمس الآيات التي هي أول ما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r2.claim: “Read, and your Lord is most generous” reassures the Prophet to proceed; God is unlike the so-called lords and will support and elevate him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r2.anchor: اقرأ وربك الأكرم على جهة التأنيس، كأنه يقول: امض لما أمرت به وربك ليس كهذه الأرباب،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176/r1.claim: Repeating 'read' reinforces the command; the verse then begins a new statement praising the Lord as supremely generous.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176/r1.anchor: اقرأ تقرير للتأكيد ثم استأنف فقال تعالى وربك الأكرم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176/r2.speaker: الخطابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176/r2.claim: Al-Akram means one whose generosity has no equal, and it can also function like 'generous,' as other superlatives mean their positive forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176/r2.anchor: الأكرم الذي لايوازيه كرم ولا يعادله في الكرم نظير وقد يكون الأكرم بمعنى الكريم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.claim: These first Qur'anic verses were the first mercy and blessing to people, reminding them of creation from a clot and God's generosity in teaching what people did not know.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.anchor: فأول شيء [نزل] (2) من القرآن هذه الآيات الكريمات المباركات (3) وهن أول رحمة رحم الله بها العباد

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and has seventeen verses.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r7.claim: Al-akram is the greatest in generosity, uniquely giving blessings no one else can provide and initiating every blessing.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r7.anchor: وهو المختص بذلك؛ إذ يعطي ما لا يقدر عليه غيره من النعم

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.speaker: عائشة ومجاهد وعطاء بن يسار
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.claim: One report says the first revelation from the Qur'an was Iqraʾ bismi rabbik.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.anchor: قيل: أول ما نزل من القرآن: (اقرأ باسم ربك)، عن عائشة، ومجاهد، وعطاء بن يسار.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.claim: Another report says the first five verses descended first, while the rest of the surah came later; a similar report is attributed to ʿĀʾisha.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.anchor: وقيل: أول ما نزل منها خمس آيات إلى قوله: (ما لم يعلم)، ثم نزل باقي السورة بعد ذلك

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r9.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r9.claim: The first “Read” commands the Prophet to read for himself and the repeated command to read for conveying the message, so it is not redundant.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r9.anchor: أما الأول: فقيل: أمر في الأولى بالقراءة لنفسه، وفي الثانية بالقراءة للتبليغ، فليس بتكرار، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r10.anchor: وقيل: كرر للتأكيد، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r11.claim: The object read is the Qur'an, or the first command concerns God's name and the second the Qur'an.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r11.anchor: وأما الثاني: فالمقروء هو القرآن، وقيل: في الأول اسمه، وفي الثاني القرآن.

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r12.claim: The Lord is creator and master; none is more generous, and because His acts benefit others one should worship Him.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r12.anchor: وربك أي: خالقك وسيدك الأكرم أي: لا أحد أكرم منه؛ لأن كل فعله إكرام وإحسان ونفع للغير

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r13.speaker: أبو علي والقاضي
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r13.claim: Abū ʿAlī says God's generosity means He will not impose without reward or beyond capacity; al-Qāḍī says He strengthens, supports, makes victorious, and steadies the Prophet.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r13.anchor: وقيل: بلغ قومك وأمتك بأنه أكرم من أن يكلفك ما لا يجازيك عليه وما لا قبل لك به، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r14.claim: Another gloss takes al-akram as the Forbearing, who does not hasten punishment.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r14.anchor: وقيل: الأكرم: الحليم عن العباد فلا يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة

KASHSHAF:96:3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:3/r1.claim: The Most Generous has unmatched generosity: He gives countless blessings, patiently delays punishment despite denial and disobedience, accepts repentance, and forgives grave sins; teaching knowledge through the pen is the highest such generosity.
KASHSHAF:96:3/r1.anchor: الذي له الكمال في زيادة كرمه على كل كرم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r6.claim: The Most Generous gives countless blessings, delays punishment, accepts repentance, and forgives grave wrongs without limit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r6.anchor: الذي له الكمال في زيادة كرمه على كل كرم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r10.anchor: اقرأ وربك الأكرم } أي الكريم . ويحتمل ثانيا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r11.claim: Alternatively, recite because your Lord is the Most Generous; the favors just mentioned evidence His generosity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r11.anchor: ويحتمل ثانيا : اقرأ بأن ربك هو الأكرم , لأنه لما ذكر ما تقدم من نعمه دل بها على نعمة كرمه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r12.speaker: إبراهيم بن عيسى اليشكري
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r12.claim: One sign of God's generosity is that He provides for a servant even while the servant worships another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r12.anchor: قال إبراهيم بن عيسى اليشكري : من كرمه أن يرزق عبده وهو يعبد غيره .

NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#6/r1.claim: The Most Generous has perfect generosity beyond every generous being, grants blessings to servants, and delays punishment despite their unbelief and denial; teaching knowledge is an especially profound generosity.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#6/r1.anchor: الذى له الكمال فى زيادة كرمه على كل كريم ينعم على عبادة النعم ويحلم عنهم

NAHHAS:v5p261/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r7.claim: The object is omitted: read what was revealed to you, and your Lord will not withhold the reward for reading.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r7.anchor: وحذف المفعول أي اقرأ ما أنزل إليك وربك الأكرم لا يخليك من الثواب على قراءتك

QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r1.claim: The second command to read is emphasis; the sentence then restarts with Lord most generous, meaning generous, as the preceding blessings demonstrate His generosity.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { اقرأ } تأكيد، وتم الكلام، ثم استأنف فقال: { وربك الأكرم } أي الكريم.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r2.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi understands the Most Generous as forbearing toward servants' ignorance and not hastening their punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يعني الحليم عن جهل العباد، فلم يعجل بعقوبتهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r3.claim: Another interpretation addresses Muhammad: read, and your Lord will help and teach you even though you are not a reader.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r3.anchor: وقيل: «إقرأ وربك» أي اقرأ يا محمد وربك يعينك ويفهمك، وإن كنت غير القارىء.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r4.claim: The word al-akram can also mean one who overlooks the ignorance of servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:3/r4.anchor: و«الأكرم» بمعنى المتجاوز عن جهل العباد.

QUTB-ZILAL:96:3/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:3/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:3/r1.claim: This verse shows God's generosity as well as power: He raises a clinging clot to a human capable of learning, an immense transformation only His power and generosity make possible.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:3/r1.anchor: فمن كرمه رفع هذا العلق إلى درجة الإنسان الذي يعلم فيتعلم

RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r1.claim: The repeated command to read may first address personal learning and then teaching others, learning from Gabriel and then instructing, or reading in prayer and outside prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : اقرأ أولا لنفسك ، والثاني للتبليغ أو الأول للتعلم من جبريل والثاني للتعليم

RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r2.claim: Generosity gives what benefits another without compensation; praise, reward, and escaping blame all count as compensation, so God cannot act to gain an end without becoming dependent and deficient.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r2.anchor: المسألة الثانية : الكرم إفادة ما ينبغي لا لعوض ، فمن يهب السكين ممن يقتل به نفسه فهو ليس بكريم

RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r3.claim: God is most generous because He increases benefaction after wrongdoing, as the cited poem says greater failure brings greater favor.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r3.anchor: أحدها : أنه كم من كريم يحلم وقت الجناية ، لكنه لا يبقى إحسانه على الوجه الذي كان قبل الجناية

RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r4.claim: God's generosity is pure, unlike human generosity that gains praise, reward, or protection from harm.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r4.anchor: أما أنا فالأكرم إذ لا أفعله إلا لمحض الكرم

RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r5.claim: He may be the most generous because He originates every kindness, whose generosity is free of deficiency.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r5.anchor: أنه الأكرم لأن له الابتداء في كل كرم وإحسان وكرمه غير مشوب بالتقصير

RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r6.claim: The title may encourage reading because God rewards each letter tenfold, urge sincerity beyond expectation, or embolden the Prophet to preach without fear because God will support him.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r6.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون هذا حثا على القراءة أي هذا الأكرم لأنه يجازيك بكل حرف عشرا

RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r7.claim: Humanity rises from the lowly clot to knowledge of realities, proving a wise governor guides this change; knowledge is the noblest human trait and God's greatest gift.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r7.anchor: أول حوال الإنسان كونه علقة وهي أخس الأشياء وآخر أمره هو صيرورته عالما بحقائق الأشياء

STUDYQURAN:96:1/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r6.claim: Pre-Islamic karāmah meant nobility and magnanimity, including noble lineage, virtuous character, and generosity.
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r6.anchor: was considered the highest of all virtues

STUDYQURAN:96:1/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r7.claim: “Most generous” is another sense: God gives creation and revelation, while Quranic use of karīm for God introduced the pagan Arabs to a new divine attribute.
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r7.anchor: this verse could also be understood to mean, “Recite, for thy Lord is most generous,”

TAB:96:3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:3/r1.claim: The command tells Muhammad to read, and describes his Lord as the Most Generous.
TAB:96:3/r1.anchor: اقْرأْ وَرَبّكَ الأكْرَمُ يقول :  اقرأ يا محمد وربك الأكرم

TAB:96:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r4.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r4.claim: Aisha recounts true dreams, Muhammad's retreat at Hira, Gabriel's arrival and repeated command to read, and identifies these opening verses as the first revelation.
TAB:96:3/r4.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت :  كان أوّل ما ابتدىء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة

TAB:96:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r5.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r5.claim: In Aisha's report, Khadija reassures Muhammad by citing his virtues; Waraqa identifies the revelation as Moses' angel, predicts opposition, and vows support if alive.
TAB:96:3/r5.anchor: فَقَالَتْ :  أبْشِرْ ،   فَوَاللّهِ لا يُخْزيكَ اللّهُ أبَدا ،   وَوَاللّهِ إنّكَ لَتَصِلُ الرّحَمِ

TAB:96:3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r6.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r6.claim: Aisha's account says that after Iqra the next revelations included Nun, the Pen, al-Muddaththir, and al-Duha.
TAB:96:3/r6.anchor: ثُمّ كانَ أوّلُ ما نَزَلَ عَليّ مِنَ القُرآنِ بَعْدَ «اقْرأْ » :  ( ن والقَلَمِ وَما يَسْطُرُونَ

TAB:96:3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
TAB:96:3/r7.claim: Ibn Shaddad reports Gabriel's reading of the opening passage, Khadija's reassurance and referral to Waraqa, then delayed revelation and al-Duha's reassurance.
TAB:96:3/r7.anchor: حدثنا عبد الله بن شدّاد ،   قال :  أتى جبريل محمدا ،   فقال :  يا محمد اقرأ

TAB:96:3/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r8.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r8.claim: Aisha, through ʿUrwa and al-Zuhri, is cited as saying the first thing revealed was ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created.’
TAB:96:3/r8.anchor: عن عائشة قال إبراهيم :  قال سفيان :  حفظه لنا ابن إسحاق :  إن أوّل شيء أُنزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r9.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r9.claim: A further report from Aisha says the first surah revealed was Iqra bi-smi rabbika.
TAB:96:3/r9.anchor: عن عائشة ،   أنّ أوّل سورة أُنزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r10.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB:96:3/r10.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says the first surah sent down to the Messenger was Iqra bi-smi rabbika alladhi khalaq.
TAB:96:3/r10.anchor: عن عُبيد بن عُمير ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r11.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
TAB:96:3/r11.claim: Abu Raja says he learned Iqra from Abu Musa al-Ashʿari and identifies it as Muhammad's first revealed surah.
TAB:96:3/r11.anchor: أبو رجاء العُطارديّ ،   قال :  كنا في المسجد الجامع ،   ومقرئنا أبو موسى الأشعريّ

TAB:96:3/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r12.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
TAB:96:3/r12.claim: ʿAta ibn Yasar says Iqra was the first surah revealed from the Qur'an.
TAB:96:3/r12.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r13.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:96:3/r13.claim: Mujahid says Iqra was the first Qur'anic revelation; one transmission adds that Nun and the Pen followed.
TAB:96:3/r13.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قال :  أوّل ما نزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ وزاد ابن مهديّ :  ن والْقَلَمِ

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r5.claim: The second command to read visibly reinforces the first.
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r5.anchor: أمر بالقراءة ثانيا تأكيدا للأمر الأول على ما هو ظاهر سياق الإطلاق

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r6.claim: One view distinguishes the commands: the first tells the Prophet to read privately and the second to recite to the people in proclamation.
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد به الأمر بالقراءة على الناس وهو التبليغ بخلاف الأمر الأول

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r7.claim: Another view takes both commands as orders to recite the Qur’an publicly.
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r7.anchor: كما قيل إن المراد بالأمرين جميعا الأمر بالقراءة على الناس

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r8.claim: Neither alternative about public recitation is apparent from the wording.

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r9.claim: The Most Generous Lord gives more than anyone else without prior entitlement; every blessing ultimately comes from Him.
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r9.anchor: فهو تعالى يعطي لا عن استحقاق وما من نعمة إلا وينتهي إيتاؤها إليه تعالى

TABRISI:96:3-10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:3-10/r1.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:96:3-10/r1.claim: The repeated command is not redundant: the first tells him to recite for himself and the second to recite for conveying the message.
TABRISI:96:3-10/r1.anchor: أمره في الأول بالقراءة لنفسه وفي الثاني بالقراءة للتبليغ وليس بتكرار عن الجبائي

TABRISI:96:3-10/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:3-10/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:3-10/r2.claim: The Lord is the most generous, whose generosity no other generous giver can match: every blessing comes from Him by creation or by providing its means.
TABRISI:96:3-10/r2.anchor: الأعظم كرما فلا يبلغه كرم كريم لأنه يعطي من النعم ما لا يقدر على مثله

TABRISI:96:3-10/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:3-10/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:96:3-10/r3.claim: Alternatively, the command is to convey the message to the people; the Most Generous rewards the Prophet, strengthens him, and helps him retain the Quran.
TABRISI:96:3-10/r3.anchor: بلغ قومك وربك الأكرم الذي يثيبك على عملك بما يقتضيه كرمه

THALABI:v10p244/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p244/r7.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v10p244/r7.claim: He glosses al-Akram as forbearing toward ignorant worship and not hastening punishment.
THALABI:v10p244/r7.anchor: قال الكلبي: يعني الحليم عن جهل العبادة ولا يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#5/r1.claim: The repeated command “Recite” reinforces certainty; the passage then resumes with God's quality of supreme generosity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#5/r1.anchor: قوله: {اقرأ} تقرير للتاكد. ثم استأنف فقال: (قوله تعالى) (¬5) {وربك الأكرم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#5/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#5/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#5/r2.claim: Al-akram means wise and forbearing toward human ignorance, not hastening punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#5/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: يعني (الحكيم) (¬6) الحليم عن جهل العباد، لا يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة

WAHIDI-QT:96:3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:3/r1.claim: God is most generous in that He bears servants' ignorance without hastening their punishment.
WAHIDI-QT:96:3/r1.anchor: { اقرأ وربك الأكرم } يعني الحليم عن جهل العباد فلا يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r4.claim: God's generosity here is His forbearance toward servants' ignorance, without hastening punishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r4.anchor: يعني: الحليم عن جهل العباد، فلا يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r12.claim: Repeating “read” confirms the first command and signals that recitation develops through practice; with what follows it also commands reciting for others or dictating.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r12.anchor: oku tekrarı ifade eden bu ikinci emir okumak melekesinin tekrar ile husûle geleceğine tenbih olmak üzere evvelkini tekid için bir tekrar olduğu gibi

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r13.claim: The syntax can make al-Akram an adjective with al-ladhi as predicate, or al-Akram the predicate and al-ladhi its adjective; either definite predicate yields exclusivity, while the first better fits the context and places prophetic honor above the pen's honor.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r13.anchor: Evvelki vecih, siyâka daha muvâfık ve nübüvvet ile ikrâmın

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r14.claim: Al-Akram describes God's limitless, gratuitous generosity and gifts and miracles; true generosity belongs to Him alone.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r14.anchor: keremine, kerâmetine nihâyet olmayan, ivazsız, garazsız, korkusuz, endişesiz lütf u hilmiyle

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.speaker: Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.claim: Beyzawi says God recounts the human's beginning and end while moving him from the lowest state to the highest, first indicating rational knowledge of God and then signifying transmitted knowledge.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.anchor: Beyzâvî der ki: “Allah sübhânehu insanı ehass-ı merâtibden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.claim: These were the first revelation; the command to read addresses Muhammad and all Muslims, and its repetition stresses the importance of reading and knowledge, through which humans are distinguished among living things.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.anchor: İlk vahyin “oku” emriyle başlaması ve bu emrin iki defa tekrar edilmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r6.claim: The third verse answers Muhammad's indirect statement that he could not read: God's limitless grace can teach through ordinary means or directly without a teacher or learning instrument.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r6.anchor: O, kullarından dilediğine, bir öğretici ve öğrenim aracılığı olmadan bilgi öğretmeye de kadirdir

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:3:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:3:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:3:anmerkung/r1.claim: Al-ʾakram may be the predicate, your Lord is most generous, or an adjective, your generous Lord is the one who teaches with the pen.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:3:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Der Ausdruck al-ʾakram lässt sich sowohl als Prädikat zu rabbuka

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:3:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:3:anmerkung/r2.speaker: Paret
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:3:anmerkung/r2.claim: Paret prefers taking al-ʾakram as an adjective, though his cited examples show that a definite elative can also function as predicate, supporting the first reading.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:3:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Obwohl Paret sich für die zweite Alternative entscheidet, führt er als Argument für die erste Q 6:133

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r4.claim: The second command to read reassures the Prophet: his Lord is unlike other lords and is the Most Generous, untouched by deficiency.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r4.anchor: ثم جاء الأمر ثانيا تأنيسا له، كأنه قيل: امض لما أمرت به، وربك ليس مثل هذه الأرباب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r5.claim: Al-akram intensifies generosity: God gives countless blessings, bears with wrongdoers, accepts repentance, and overlooks sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r5.anchor: والأكرم صفة تدل على المبالغة في الكرم، إذ كرمه يزيد على كل كرم ينعم بالنعم التي لا تحصى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r9.claim: The author condemns Christians' use of divine epithets such as al-Akram and al-Rashid as names for people, calling this shameful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r9.anchor: ومن غريب ما رأينا تسمية النصارى بهذه الصفة التي هي صفة لله تعالى: الأكرم، والرشيد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#2/r1.claim: The repeated command reinforces the obligation and prepares the way for the next statement about God's generosity, removing the Prophet's excuse that reading belongs to literate people; the command is to read beginning in God's name.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#2/r1.anchor: اقرأ أي افعل ما أمرت به تأكيدا للأيجاب وتمهيدا لما يعقبه من قوله تعالى وربك الأكرم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r3.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r3.claim: Al-Jubbai says the first Read commands personal reading or reading generally, while the second is reading for proclamation; another view connects the latter to prayer, and the Lord's generosity clause could be circumstantial or independent.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r3.anchor: ولجبائي أن اقرأ الأول أمر بالقراءة لنفسه وقيل مطلقا والثاني أمر بالقراءة للتبليغ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r4.claim: If the reading is for proclamation, the command means to tell one's people that the generous Lord rewards work, strengthens the Prophet to retain the Quran, and enables its delivery.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r4.anchor: وحاصل المعنى على إرادة القراءة للتبليغ في قول بلغ قومك وربك الأكرم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r5.claim: Al-Alusi says the clearest interpretation is that the second Read reinforces the first; the proposal to attach the basmala's باسم to the second command to make God's name the exclusive starting point is far-fetched because it normally attaches to the adjacent command.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r5.anchor: وأولى الأوجه وأظهرها التأكيد وأبعد بعضهم جدا فزعم أن بسم في البسملة متعلق باقرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r6.claim: The fronted command suits the importance of reading in the first surah revealed; even if another passage preceded it, the sense is read beginning with God's name, so other openings would not comply, while moving the name first changes the focus.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الظاهر تعلق باسم ربك بما عنده وتقديم الفعل ههنا أوقع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r6.claim: Some scholars object to calling people most generous in correspondence, even though they regard it as modest praise for rulers, and criticize applying it to Jews or Christians; people should show reverence and gratitude for the generosity of their Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r6.anchor: ولم ير بعض العلماء من الأدب وصف غيره تعالى كما يفعله كثير من الناس في رسائلهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.claim: Most commentators say this was the first sura revealed and that its first five verses, through the words about what humanity did not know, were the first revelation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.anchor: أكثر المفسرين: على أن هذه السورة أول سورة نزلت من القرآن، وأول ما نزل خمس آيات من أولها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.claim: Aisha says revelation began with true dreams and retreat to Hira; Gabriel commanded the Prophet to read and squeezed him three times before reciting these verses; he returned frightened and Khadija reassured him through his virtues.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت: أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة في النوم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.claim: Khadija brought the Prophet to Waraqa, who identified the visitor as the messenger sent to Moses, predicted his people would expel him, and promised support before dying as revelation paused.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.anchor: فانطلقت به خديجة حتى أتت به ورقة بن نوفل بن أسد بن عبد العزى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r3.claim: The repeated command to read serves as emphasis; the phrase about the Most Generous Lord begins a fresh clause.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r3.anchor: اقرأ} كرره تأكيدا، ثم استأنف فقال: {وربك الأكرم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r4.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi explains God's generosity as forbearance toward servants' ignorance: He does not hasten to punish them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r4.anchor: فقال الكلبي: الحليم عن جهل العباد لا يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r5.claim: The second command to recite either intensifies the first, or distinguishes unrestricted recitation from proclamation or reciting in prayer; it may follow the Prophet's response “I cannot read.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r5.anchor: تكرير للمبالغة، أو الأول مطلق والثاني للتبليغ أو في الصلاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r6.claim: God is more generous than every generous person because He gives without compensation and forbears without fear; He alone is truly generous.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r6.anchor: الزائد في الكرم على كل كريم فإنه سبحانه وتعالى ينعم بلا عوض

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.claim: God recounts humanity's beginning and destination to show the favor of raising it from the lowest rank to the highest, affirm His lordship and generosity, and move from rational proof to sensory evidence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.anchor: وقد عدد سبحانه وتعالى مبدأ أمر الإنسان ومنتهاه إظهارا لما أنعم عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.claim: She presents the surah’s opening as the first revelation, noting that Ibn Ishaq and al-Tabari report no disagreement about that account.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.anchor: والمشهور كذلك أنه أمل سورة نزلت من الوحي. ولم يشر "ابن إسحاق" في (السيرة النبوية) إلي خلاف

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.claim: Aisha recounts Muhammad’s true dreams, retreat to Hira, Gabriel’s command and three embraces, and the recitation of the opening five verses, which remained fixed in his heart; no grading is stated.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.anchor: عن "السيدة عائشة أم المؤمنين" قالت: "كان أول ما ابتدئ به رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من الوحي

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.claim: Aisha continues that Muhammad saw Gabriel in the sky, returned to Khadija, and was reassured because his character included kinship, truthfulness, trustworthiness, hospitality, and helping in adversity; no grading is stated.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.anchor: فقالت: أبشر يا ابن عم واثبت، فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبداً، إنك لتصل الرحم وتصدق الحديث

BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.claim: Al-Razi also transmits that only al-Alaq’s first five verses came at the start; the remainder came after public opposition and were joined to the surah by God’s command.
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.anchor: أن الذي نزل من السورة أول الوحي، آياتها الخمس الأولى

BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.claim: Al-Bahr al-Muhit says the surah is Meccan and its opening was the first revelation at Hira, as established in Bukhari and elsewhere; it judges the claims that al-Muddaththir or the Fatiha came first unsound.
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.anchor: وقول جابر: أول ما نزل المدثر، وقول أبي ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل: أول ما نزل الفاتحة، لا يصح

BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.claim: The reports in al-Tabari and the Prophetic biography stop the first-revelation account at verse five, supporting the view that the opening alone was first revealed.
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.anchor: حيث يقف الحديث فيهما عن اول ما نزل من الوحي، عند الآية الخامسة

BINTSHATI:v2p20/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r1.claim: Some exegetes, as al-Razi transmits, say the first اقرأ is for the Prophet himself and the second for proclamation to others.
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r1.anchor: أن {اقْرَأْ} في الآية الأولى تعني: "اقرأ لنفسك، وهي في هذه الآية بمعنى التبليغ

BINTSHATI:v2p20/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r2.claim: A second reported interpretation makes the first command to read for learning and the second to teach.
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r2.anchor: أو أن الأولى للتعلم، والثانية للتعليم

BINTSHATI:v2p20/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r3.claim: A third reported interpretation says the first recitation is in prayer and the second outside prayer.
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r3.anchor: أو أن الأولى: اقرأ في صلاتك، والثانية: اقرأ خارج صلاتك

BINTSHATI:v2p20/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r4.claim: She prefers the straightforward context: the command to recite is reiterated, and revelation specifies what the Prophet should read in his Lord’s name.
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r4.anchor: وهي أقوال متقاربة، وإن كان الأولى لأخذ السياق على ظاهره، بما يفيد من تأكيد الأمر الإلهي

BINTSHATI:v2p20/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r5.claim: In Arabic, karam is the opposite of baseness and suggests honor; ikram is the opposite of humiliation and degradation.
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r5.anchor: والكرم في العربية نقيض اللؤم، ودلالته على العزة مألوفة

BINTSHATI:v2p20/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r6.claim: The Quran applies karim to God, His throne, a messenger, an angel, scripture, and the promised provision, reward, abode, and station of the righteous.
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r6.anchor: كما جاء وصفاً لرسول، وملك، وكتاب، وقرآن كريم، ووعد المتقون برزق، وأجر، ومدخل ومقام كريم

BINTSHATI:v2p20/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r7.claim: In a threatening, ironic address to the sinner, the Quran calls him العزيز الكريم as he is led to Hell.
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r7.anchor: وفي سياق الوعيد والسخرية، جاءت آية الدخان في الأثيم

BINTSHATI:v2p21/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r1.claim: God’s honoring of the righteous is contrasted with His humiliating whom He wills; in al-Hujurat, akramakum is restricted to the addressed human community.
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r1.anchor: أما أفعل التفضيل، فجاء مرة مضافاً إلى ضمير المخاطبين في آية الحجرات

BINTSHATI:v2p21/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains al-Akram as God’s unsurpassed generosity: He gives countless gifts, is patient with disbelief, accepts repentance, and forgives grave sins.
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r2.anchor: الذي له الكمال زيادة كرمه على كل كرم، ينعم على عباده النعم التي لا تحصى

BINTSHATI:v2p21/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r3.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r3.claim: Al-Razi says God not only forbears when people sin but increases His kindness afterward; a cited poem makes the point that greater failure brings greater favor.
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r3.anchor: أنه تعالى لا يحلن وقت جناية الإنسان فحسب، بل يزيد إحسانه بعد الجناية

BINTSHATI:v2p21/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r4.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r4.claim: Al-Razi’s second explanation contrasts Muhammad’s generosity with the greater generosity of his Lord.
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r4.anchor: أنك كريم يا محمد، لكن ربك الأكرم

BINTSHATI:v2p21/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r5.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r5.claim: Al-Razi also says God originates every generosity and kindness, and His generosity is free of any shortcoming.
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r5.anchor: أنه تعالى له الابتداء في كل كرم وإحسان، وكرمه غير مشوب بتقصير

BINTSHATI:v2p21/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r6.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r6.claim: One further reading urges recitation by promising ten rewards for each Quranic letter.
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r6.anchor: فهو يجازيك بكل حرف مما تقرأ عشراً

BINTSHATI:v2p21/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r7.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r7.claim: Alternatively, al-Razi reads al-Akram as reassurance to proclaim the message without fear because God will support the Prophet in this strenuous mission.
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r7.anchor: تجرد لدعوة الخلق ولا تخف أحداً، فأنا أكرم من أن آمرك بهذا التكليف الشافي ثم لا أنصرك

BINTSHATI:v2p21/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r8.claim: She rejects limiting al-Akram to comparison among finite beings: the definite, unqualified form claims absolute, unrestricted supremacy for God, unlike the human comparison in al-Hujurat.
BINTSHATI:v2p21/r8.anchor: والحق أن البيان القرآني حين قيد أفعل التفضيل في آية الحجرات بإضافتها إلى ضمير المخاطبين

BINTSHATI:v2p22/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p22/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p22/r1.claim: An Arabic superlative made definite with al and left unspecified conveys an absolute general sense; with a complement or specification, comparison remains limited to that scope.
BINTSHATI:v2p22/r1.anchor: أفعل التفضيل معرفاً بأل، وغير مميز، فتفيد من العموم والإطلاق ما لا تفيده الصيغة نفسها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p481/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p481/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p481/r4.claim: God's being al-Akram means absolute perfection in essence, attributes, and acts, free of every deficiency, and the source of gifts beyond measure.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p481/r4.anchor: الذي له الكمال الأعظم مطلقا من جهة الذات ومن جهة الصفات ومن جهة الأفعال

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.claim: The author classifies the chapter as Meccan and counts nineteen verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.claim: Aisha's account describes true dreams and retreat at Hira before Gabriel commands him to read, presses him three times, and recites the first five verses; Muhammad returns trembling to Khadija.
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت: أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة في النوم

ITQAN:v3p284/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.claim: The opening of “Read” similarly previews the Qur’an: it commands reading, begins in God’s name, signals legal knowledge and the principles of religion, and reports God’s teaching of what humans did not know; it can therefore be called the Qur’an’s title.
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.anchor: وكذلك أول سورة ( اقرأ فإنها مشتملة على نظير ما اشتملت عليه الفاتحة من براعة الاستهلال

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha says revelation began with true dreams and seclusion at Ḥirāʾ; Gabriel's repeated commands to recite introduced al-ʿAlaq, and the shaken Prophet was comforted by Khadīja, who cited his virtues. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت: "أول ما بدئ به رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.speaker: بعض علمائهم
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.claim: Ibn Shihāb relays from Muḥammad b. ʿAbbād that some scholars said al-ʿAlaq's first five verses were revealed at Ḥirāʾ; the remainder came later as God willed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.anchor: أنه سمع بعض علمائهم يقول: كان أول ما أنزل الله على رسوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r1.speaker: الملاحدة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r1.claim: Heretics argued, as al-Razi notes, that calling God “the Highest” would imply another, lesser lord by the logic of comparison.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r1.anchor: "افخر الرازي" من تعلق الملاحدة في "ربه الأعلى" من اقتضاء أن يكون هناك رب آخر مفضولاً في العلو

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r2.claim: Bint al-Shati rejects that comparative reading: an unqualified form such as “the Highest” expresses the utmost degree of height without limit or comparison.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r2.anchor: وإنما القصد إلى المضي بالعلو إلى نهايته القصوى بغير حدود ولا قيود

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r3.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r3.claim: Some commentators treated al-akram as a comparison with karīm and offered several grounds for God’s greater generosity; Bint al-Shati rejects this and says the form is not chosen merely for rhyme.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r3.anchor: لم يعدل فيها عن الكريم إلى الأكرم، لمجرد رعاية الفاصلة، ولا قصد بها المفاضلة بين أكرم وكريم، على ما تأوله مفسرون

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r4.claim: The forms afʿal and fuʿlā express an unrestricted maximum; comparison is specified when a comparator is named, such as with an explicit مِنْ or a stated object.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r4.anchor: إنما تتعين المفاضلة بذكر المفضول، مضافا إليه أو مجرورا بحرف من، في مثل: أكثر الناس، أكثركم، أكبر من أختها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r5.claim: “God is the best of plotters” is genuinely comparative in context, because it answers the plotting of human opponents, including Thamud and the disbelievers among the Israelites.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p272/r5.anchor: ووجه التفضيل في مثل قوله تعالى: {وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ} أنه في سياق الحديث عن مكر المخلوقين: ثمود في آية (النمل 50)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p274/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p274/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p274/r1.claim: Without a stated comparator or limit, afʿal and fuʿlā forms carry an unbounded sense of the utmost, as in al-akram and Quranic expressions for the greatest sign, blow, calamity, fire, and model.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p274/r1.anchor: فإذا أطلق "الأفعل، والفُعلى" من قيد ومن مفضول، خرج، والله أعلم، عن دلالة المفاضلة وخصوصية القيد، وأفاد الإطلاق غير المحدود

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p274/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p274/r2.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p274/r2.claim: Al-Farra held that the two gardens in 55:46 were really one, with the dual chosen for cadence; Bint al-Shati rejects this because the surrounding passage consistently addresses two gardens for humans and jinn.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p274/r2.anchor: ليست تثنية جنتين فيها مراداً بها الإفراد وعدل القرآن إليها مراعاة للنظم كما ذعهب "الفراء"

IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.speaker: عبيد
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.claim: Ubayd's report says Muhammad annually secluded himself at Hira during Ramadan, fed the poor, and returned to circumambulate the Kaaba; Gabriel then came with a written silk cloth and commanded him to recite, repeating the embrace three times, after which Muhammad woke with the words fixed in his heart.
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.anchor: قال عبيد: فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجاور ذلك الشهر من كل سنة، يطعم من جاءه من المساكين

ABUHAYYAN:96:3/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:3/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:3/r1.claim: The command is repeated to reassure the Prophet to continue, since his Lord is unlike the pagan lords and is free of deficiency.
ABUHAYYAN:96:3/r1.anchor: ثم جاء الأمر ثانياً تأنيساً له ، كأنه قيل : امض لما أمرت به ، وربك ليس مثل هذه الأرباب

ABUHAYYAN:96:3/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:3/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:3/r2.claim: Al-Akram is an intensive description of God's surpassing generosity: He grants uncountable blessings, bears with wrongdoers, accepts repentance, and overlooks sin.
ABUHAYYAN:96:3/r2.anchor: والأكرم صفة تدل على المبالغة في الكرم ، إذ كرمه يزيد على كل كرم ينعم بالنعم التي لا تحصى ،

ABUHAYYAN:96:4/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:4/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:4/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects to Christians using God's attributes such as al-Akram and al-Rashid as honorific names, and warns of the shameful consequence when words and deeds are presented.
ABUHAYYAN:96:4/r6.anchor: ومن غريب ما رأينا تسمية النصارى بهذه الصفة التي هي صفة لله تعالى : الأكرم ، والرشيد ، وفخر السعداء ، وسعيد السعداء ، والشيخ الرشيد

ALUSI:96:3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:3/r1.claim: Repeating the command to recite reinforces its obligation and prepares for the following declaration of the Lord’s generosity.
ALUSI:96:3/r1.anchor: أي افعل ما أمرت به تأكيداً للإيجاب وتمهيداً لما يعقبه

ALUSI:96:3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:3/r2.claim: The declaration about the Lord’s generosity is a new, independent sentence, intended to remove the Prophet’s stated excuse.
ALUSI:96:3/r2.anchor: فإنه كلام مستأنف وأراد لإزاحة ما بينه صلى الله عليه وسلم من العذر

ALUSI:96:3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:3/r3.claim: The Prophet told Gabriel, “I am not a reader,” explaining that reading belonged to one who writes and reads while he was unlettered; no grading is given.
ALUSI:96:3/r3.anchor: يريد أن القراءة شأن من يكتب ويقرأ وأنا أمي

ALUSI:96:3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:3/r4.claim: The answer is that the Lord who commanded recitation, beginning with His name, is the Most Generous.
ALUSI:96:3/r4.anchor: فقيل وربك الذي أمرك بالقراءة مفتتحاً ومبتدأ باسمه الأكرم

ALUSI:96:4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:4/r2.claim: Alternatively, the second recite is not a mere repetition but introduces the clause that removes the excuse; the Lord clause is circumstantial to its implicit subject.
ALUSI:96:4/r2.anchor: هذا تأكيداً للأول وإنما ذكر ليوصل به ما يزيح العذر فجملة

ALUSI:96:5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r5.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI:96:5/r5.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the first command is to recite for oneself.

ALUSI:96:5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:5/r6.claim: Another view takes the first command to mean recitation without specifying that it is for oneself.
ALUSI:96:5/r6.anchor: وقيل مطلقاً والثاني أمر بالقراءة للتبليغ

ALUSI:96:5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:5/r7.claim: One view takes the second command as recitation for conveying the message.

ALUSI:96:5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:5/r8.claim: Another view connects the second command with recitation in the prayer referred to later.
ALUSI:96:5/r8.anchor: وقيل في الصلاة المشار إليها فيما بعد

ALUSI:96:5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:5/r9.claim: The clause about the Lord may be read either as circumstantial or as an independent sentence.

ALUSI:96:5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:5/r10.claim: If recitation is for conveying, the Prophet is to proclaim to his people that his generous Lord rewards him and strengthens him to memorize and deliver the Qur’an.
ALUSI:96:5/r10.anchor: الذي يثيبك على عملك بما يقتضيه كرمه ويقويك على حفظ القرآن لتبلغه

ALUSI:96:5/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r11.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:5/r11.claim: A very remote analysis attaches “in the name” in the basmala to the first recite and “in your Lord’s name” to the second, making the fronting specify God’s name as the required opening.
ALUSI:96:5/r11.anchor: وأبعد بعضهم جداً فزعم أن بسم في البسملة متعلق باقرأ الأول

ALUSI:96:5/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:5/r12.claim: Another analysis leaves “in God’s name” with its customary attachment, treats recite as initiating the reading, and attaches “your Lord” to the second command.
ALUSI:96:5/r12.anchor: وجوز أيضاً أن يبقى باسم الله على ما هو المشهور فيه

ALUSI:96:5/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:5/r13.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers attaching “in your Lord’s name” to the adjacent verb; placing the verb first suits this opening surah, where recitation is especially important.
ALUSI:96:5/r13.anchor: تعلق { باسم رَبّكَ } بما عنده وتقديم الفعل ههنا أوقع

ALUSI:96:5/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r14.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI:96:5/r14.claim: Qatāda explains the command as beginning in the Lord’s name: say “In God’s name,” then recite; without the basmala, or with an idol’s name, the command would not be fulfilled.
ALUSI:96:5/r14.anchor: فلو افتتح بغير البسملة لم يكن ممتثلاً فضلاً عن أن يفتتح

ALUSI:96:5/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:5/r15.claim: Fronting the prepositional phrase would instead make opening in God’s name the requested act, while recitation itself would be presupposed rather than commanded.
ALUSI:96:5/r15.anchor: ولو قدم الجار أفاد معنى آخر وهو أن المطلوب عند القراءة أن يكون الافتتاح باسم الله تعالى لا باسم الأصنام ولا تكون القراءة في نفسها مطلوبة

ALUSI:96:5/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r16.speaker: من علق الجار بالثاني
ALUSI:96:5/r16.claim: Those attaching the phrase to the second command answer that the first command already establishes recitation itself as required.
ALUSI:96:5/r16.anchor: وأجاب من علق الجار بالثاني بأن مطلوبية القراءة في نفسها استفيدت من اقرأ الأول

ALUSI:96:5/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r29.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:5/r29.claim: Some scholars consider it discourteous to call anyone but God “the Most Generous,” even though people use it for correspondents, rulers, and non-Muslims; servants should honor their Lord and thank Him for His generosity.
ALUSI:96:5/r29.anchor: ولم ير بعض العلماء من الأدب وصف غيره تعالى بالأكرم كما يفعله كثير من الناس في رسائلهم فيكتبون إلى فلان الأكرم

BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.claim: Most commentators hold that this was the first sūra revealed and that the first revelation was its opening five verses, ending with “what he did not know.”
BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.anchor: أكثر المفسرين : على أن هذه السورة أول سورة نزلت من القرآن ، وأول ما نزل خمس آيات

BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.claim: Aisha recounts the Prophet’s true dreams, retreat and worship at Hira, then Gabriel’s command to read and three forceful embraces before reciting the opening revelation; Baghawi gives no grading.
BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت : " أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة

BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.claim: After the revelation the frightened Prophet returned to Khadija, who reassured him that God would never disgrace him because he maintained kinship, supported the needy, hosted guests, and aided people in hardship.
BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.anchor: فقالت خديجة : كلا ، والله ما يخزيك الله أبداً ، إنك لتصل الرحم ، وتحمل الكل ، وتكسب المعدوم

BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.speaker: الزهري
BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.claim: In a Bukhari version, al-Zuhri adds that revelation paused and the Prophet, in grief, repeatedly approached mountain peaks intending to throw himself down until Gabriel reassured him; the addition is introduced as “what reached us.”
BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.anchor: حتى حزن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما بلغنا حزناً غدا منه مراراً حتى يتردى من رؤوس شواهق الجبال

BAGHAWI:96:3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:3/r1.claim: The command to read is repeated for emphasis, after which the verse begins a new statement about the Lord’s generosity.
BAGHAWI:96:3/r1.anchor: اقرأ } كرره تأكيداً ، ثم استأنف فقال : { وربك الأكرم }

BAGHAWI:96:3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:3/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI:96:3/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi explains the Most Generous as forbearing toward people’s ignorance and not hastening their punishment.
BAGHAWI:96:3/r2.anchor: فقال الكلبي : الحليم عن جهل العباد لا يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة

BAYDAWI:96:3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:3/r1.claim: Knowledge of God is the first obligation; the opening revelation first points to His existence, immense power, and complete wisdom.
BAYDAWI:96:3/r1.anchor: ولما كان أول الواجبات معرفة الله سبحانه وتعالى

BAYDAWI:96:3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:3/r2.claim: The repeated command may emphasize the first, distinguish general reading from conveying or prayer, or answer the Prophet's “I cannot read.”

BAYDAWI:96:3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:3/r3.claim: God exceeds every generous giver: He grants without compensation and is forbearing without fear; He alone is truly generous.
BAYDAWI:96:3/r3.anchor: الزائد في الكرم على كل كريم

BIQAI:96:3/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:3/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:3/r1.claim: The repeated reading command marks a shift from gradual creation through causes to origination without causes; it emphasizes reading, reassures Muhammad, calms his fear, and distinguishes its sender from their lords.
BIQAI:96:3/r1.anchor: ولما أتم سبحانه ما أراد من أمر الخلق وهو الإيجاد بالأسباب بالتدريج

BIQAI:96:3/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:3/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:3/r2.claim: One implied construction is that the Lord who nurtured and trained Muhammad commands him to read and can make him read; alternatively, the phrase is circumstantial, stressing that his benefactor is supremely generous.

BIQAI:96:3/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:3/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:3/r3.claim: God is absolutely most perfect in essence, attributes, and acts, without deficiency; He gathers the highest virtues and gives beyond measure.

DURR:96:1/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r3.speaker: بعض علمائهم
DURR:96:1/r3.claim: Scholars heard by Muḥammad b. ʿAbbād said the opening through 96:5 was revealed at Ḥirāʾ; the sūra’s ending came later as God willed.
DURR:96:1/r3.anchor: عن ابن شهاب : حدثني محمد بن عباد بن جعفر المخزومي أنه سمع بعض علمائهم يقول

DURR:96:1/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r6.speaker: عائشة
DURR:96:1/r6.claim: In ʿĀʾisha’s account, Gabriel commanded the unlettered Prophet to recite, squeezed him three times, then delivered the opening five verses at Ḥirāʾ.
DURR:96:1/r6.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت : «أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة

DURR:96:1/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:1/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the first revelation consisted of five verses, ending with “what he did not know.”
DURR:96:1/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : أول شيء أنزل من القرآن خمس آيات { اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق } إلى قوله : { ما لم يعلم } .

DURR:96:1/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r15.speaker: الزهري وعمرو بن دينار
DURR:96:1/r15.claim: Al-Zuhrī and ʿAmr b. Dīnār report that, at Ḥirāʾ, an angel brought the Prophet brocade bearing the opening five verses in writing.
DURR:96:1/r15.anchor: عن الزهري وعمرو بن دينار أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذا أتاه ملك بنمط من ديباج

DURR:96:1/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r16.speaker: عمرو بن جابر
DURR:96:1/r16.claim: ʿAmr b. Jābir likewise reports that an angel came to the Prophet at Ḥirāʾ with brocade inscribed through “what he did not know.”
DURR:96:1/r16.anchor: من طريق عمرو بن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذ أتاه ملك

DURR:96:1/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r17.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
DURR:96:1/r17.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Shaddād recounts Gabriel’s repeated command to recite and squeezing of Muhammad, who then received the opening passage through 96:5.
DURR:96:1/r17.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شداد قال : «أتى جبريل محمداً صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : يا محمد اقرأ

DURR:96:1/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r19.speaker: عائشة
DURR:96:1/r19.claim: A second ʿĀʾisha account describes Gabriel’s vast appearance, washing the Prophet’s opened chest, teaching the opening five verses, and weighing him against men; Michael says his community will follow.
DURR:96:1/r19.anchor: عن عائشة «أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اعتكف هو وخديجة شهراً فوافق ذلك رمضان

IBNATIYYA:96:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:3/r1.claim: The command reassures the Prophet to proceed: his Lord is unlike the idols, supremely generous and free of deficiency, and will support and make him prevail.
IBNATIYYA:96:3/r1.anchor: على جهة التأنيس ،   كأنه يقول : امض لما أمرت به وربك ليس كهذه الأرباب ،   بل هو الأكرم

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that true dreams began revelation, then the Prophet loved solitude, worshiped at Ḥirāʾ for several nights, and Khadīja supplied his provisions.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r3.claim: ʿĀʾisha recounts Gabriel's three forceful embraces in the cave, Muhammad's repeated reply that he could not read, and Gabriel's recitation of the opening revelation; Muhammad returned trembling.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r3.anchor: فجاءه الملك فيه فقال : اقرأ . قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r4.speaker: خديجة
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r4.claim: In ʿĀʾisha's report, Khadīja reassures Muhammad that God will never disgrace him, citing his kinship ties, truthfulness, bearing burdens, hospitality, and help in adversity.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r4.anchor: يا خديجة ، ما لي : فأخبرها الخبر وقال : " قد خشيت علي " . فقالت له : كلا أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا ؛ إنك لتصل الرحم

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r5.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r5.claim: Waraqa ibn Nawfal, Khadīja's relative, was a pre-Islamic Christian who wrote Arabic and Gospel material in it; he identified the angel as the messenger sent to Moses, predicted opposition and expulsion, and promised support if alive.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r5.anchor: فقال ورقة : هذا الناموس الذي أنزل على موسى

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr adds, with the qualifier “as has reached us,” that after Waraqa's death revelation paused and grief brought Muhammad repeatedly to mountain peaks, where Gabriel reassured him he was truly God's messenger.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r6.anchor: وفَتَر الوحي فترة حتى حَزن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم - فيما بلغنا -

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the report is transmitted in both Ṣaḥīḥs through al-Zuhrī; he notes that he examined its chain, text, and meanings in his Bukhārī commentary.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r7.anchor: وهذا الحديث مخرج في الصحيحين من حديث الزهري

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r8.claim: Ibn Kathīr says these opening verses are God's first mercy to humanity and His first blessing upon them.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r8.anchor: وهُنَّ أول رحمة رَحم الله بها العباد

MAWARDI:96:3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:3/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:3/r2.claim: Alternatively, read it as recite knowing that your Lord is the Most Generous: the blessings just mentioned point to His generosity.
MAWARDI:96:3/r2.anchor: ويحتمل ثانياً : اقرأ بأن ربك هو الأكرم ،   لأنه لما ذكر ما تقدم من نعمه دل بها على نعمة كرمه

MAWARDI:96:3/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:3/r3.speaker: إبراهيم بن عيسى اليشكري
MAWARDI:96:3/r3.claim: Ibrāhīm ibn ʿĪsā al-Yashkurī illustrates God's generosity by saying He provides for His servant while the servant worships another.
MAWARDI:96:3/r3.anchor: قال إبراهيم بن عيسى اليشكري : من كرمه أن يرزق عبده وهو يعبد غيره

NASAFI:96:3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:3/r1.claim: Al-Akram describes the Lord's complete generosity, surpassing every other generous giver.
NASAFI:96:3/r1.anchor: { اقرأ وَرَبُّكَ الأكرم } الذي له الكمال في زيادة كرمه على كل كريم

NASAFI:96:3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:3/r2.claim: He bestows favors on His servants and bears with their unbelief and ingratitude, delaying punishment; teaching knowledge is the supreme generosity of imparting benefits.
NASAFI:96:3/r2.anchor: باده النعم ويحلم عنهم ، فلا يعاجلهم

QURTUBI:96:3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:3/r1.claim: The repeated command confirms the first; that sentence is complete, and a new sentence begins with your Lord is most generous.
QURTUBI:96:3/r1.anchor: " اقرأ " تأكيد ، وتم الكلام ، ثم استأنف فقال : " وربك الأكرم "

QURTUBI:96:3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:3/r2.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI:96:3/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the Most Generous as forbearing toward servants' ignorance and not hastening to punish them.
QURTUBI:96:3/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي : يعني الحليم عن جهل العباد ، فلم يعجل بعقوبتهم .

QURTUBI:96:3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:3/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the ordinary sense generous, since the blessings just mentioned demonstrate God's generosity.
QURTUBI:96:3/r3.anchor: والأول أشبه بالمعنى ، لأنه لما ذكر ما تقدم من نعمه ، دل بها على كرمه .

QURTUBI:96:3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:3/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:3/r4.claim: Another reading of the phrase addresses Muhammad: read, and your Lord will help and teach you even though you cannot read.
QURTUBI:96:3/r4.anchor: وقيل : " اقرأ وربك " أي اقرأ يا محمد وربك يعينك ويفهمك

QURTUBI:96:3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:3/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:3/r5.claim: A further gloss takes al-akram to mean the One who overlooks servants' ignorance.
QURTUBI:96:3/r5.anchor: و " الأكرم " بمعنى المتجاوز عن جهل العباد .

RAZI:96:3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI:96:3/r1.claim: Some say the first command to read is for oneself and the second for communicating; alternatively, they are learning from Gabriel then teaching, or reading in prayer then outside it.

RAZI:96:3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r2.claim: Generosity is giving what is fitting without compensation; a gift later repaid by praise, reward, or escape from blame is not wholly free of recompense.
RAZI:96:3/r2.anchor: الكرم إفادة ما ينبغي لا لعوض

RAZI:96:3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI:96:3/r3.claim: Rāzī’s school argues God cannot act for an end: gaining a preferred outcome would mean He improves through an act and was deficient without it.
RAZI:96:3/r3.anchor: قال أصحابنا : إنه تعالى يستحيل أن يفعل فعلا لغرض

RAZI:96:3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r4.claim: One account of God’s greater generosity is that He increases beneficence after an offense, unlike a person whose kindness may diminish; a cited poem voices this.

RAZI:96:3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r5.claim: A second account: other generous people benefit through praise, reward, or averting harm, whereas God gives from pure generosity alone.
RAZI:96:3/r5.anchor: أما أنا فالأكرم إذ لا أفعله إلا لمحض الكرم

RAZI:96:3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r6.claim: A third account calls God most generous because He initiates every generosity and beneficence, and His generosity is untainted by deficiency.
RAZI:96:3/r6.anchor: له الابتداء في كل كرم وإحسان وكرمه غير مشوب

RAZI:96:3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r7.claim: One possible exhortation is to read because God rewards each letter tenfold.
RAZI:96:3/r7.anchor: أي هذا الأكرم لأنه يجازيك بكل حرف عشرا

RAZI:96:3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r8.claim: Another possible exhortation is to read sincerely for God rather than from appetite, entrusting one’s request to the One who gives beyond expectation.
RAZI:96:3/r8.anchor: لا تقرأ لطمع ولكن لأجلي ودع علي أمرك

RAZI:96:3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r9.claim: The wording may also encourage the Prophet to devote himself to calling people without fear: God would not impose this hard task and then withhold support.
RAZI:96:3/r9.anchor: تجرد لدعوة الخلق ولا تخف أحدا فأنا أكرم

RAZI:96:3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r10.claim: The movement from the human’s lowly beginning as a clot to the highest created rank, knowledge, shows a directing and determining Lord; knowledge is humanity’s noblest trait.
RAZI:96:3/r10.anchor: أول أحوال الإنسان كونه علقة وهي أخس الأشياء

RAZI:96:3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r11.claim: Creation, life, power, and provision are generosity and lordship; the highest generosity is granting knowledge, the most exalted human distinction.
RAZI:96:3/r11.anchor: الإيجاد والإحياء والإقدار والرزق كرم وربوبية

RAZI:96:3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r12.claim: The opening reference to the Lord who created humanity from a clot provides a rational proof of divine power, wisdom, knowledge, and mercy.
RAZI:96:3/r12.anchor: الدلالة العقلية الدالة على كمال القدرة والحكمة والعلم والرحمة
